head: bf662f8
target: Ship the gate as one plugin for Claude Code, Droid, and Codex, so every clone of an opted-in repo gets the gate with no manual setup and an agent cannot bypass it.
incidental: the rewritten selftest: scaffolding that covers the new hooks and the gate
manifest metadata: plugin names, version, owner, and descriptions
the installer's source override and its closing message
the message-by-message plumbing inside the Codex trust step

questions.prompt: The skill ships as one plugin. What lets the same package install into Claude Code, Droid, and Codex?

options.label: All three read the same plugin manifests and the same hooks file.
The installer rewrites the hooks in each tool's own format.
The tools all run bash, so the packaging does not matter.

key_points: The three tools read the same plugin manifests and the same hooks declarations.
One shared format serves all three; per-tool copies would drift.

questions.prompt: A pre-push hook lives in each clone, not in the plugin. Why does the plugin install it when a session starts, not when the plugin is installed?

options.label: Install time reaches the user once; session start reaches every clone as it opens.
Hooks written at install time would vanish with each plugin update.
Session start is the only hook event all three tools support.

key_points: The plugin is installed once per user, but the hook must exist in every clone.
Session start reaches each clone as it opens, so a fresh clone needs no setup.
Session start also keeps the gate tool on PATH.

questions.prompt: The guard sees each shell command the agent wants to run. Which of these does it deny?

options.label: A push that tells git to skip its hooks
A command that points git at a different hooks folder
A plain push of commits with no passed quiz
A command that only reads the hooks folder setting

key_points: The guard denies pushes that skip hooks and commands that move git's hooks folder.
A plain push passes the guard; the pre-push hook blocks it later.
Bypassing the gate is the human's call, never the agent's.
The guard checks command text, so it stops the plain bypasses, not every trick.

questions.prompt: Codex skips a plugin's hooks until it trusts them. What does the installer do about this?

options.label: It writes the trust entries Codex itself writes when you approve a hook.
It asks the user to approve each hook the first time it runs.
It tells Codex to run the hooks without trusting them first.

key_points: Codex runs a plugin hook only when its hash is on its trust list.
The installer writes the same trust entries the approval step writes.
Without this step, the hooks install but never run in Codex.

questions.prompt: The session-start hook fails on a user's machine. What happens to their next session?

options.label: The session starts normally; the hook's error never reaches it.
The session starts, but the plugin is listed as broken.
Session start fails until the user fixes the error.

key_points: The hook never fails the session; it swallows its own errors.
Worst case, the gate is missing in that clone, not the session.

questions.prompt: Which of these does the plugin do?

options.label: In a repo with the opt-in marker, session start installs the pre-push hook.
In a repo without the marker, session start still prints the gate warning.
The installer replaces a pre-push hook the repo already had.
When a repo already has a hook, the install fails and names the line to add.

key_points: Only a repo with the tracked opt-in marker gets the hook and the warning.
The marker is tracked in the repo, so it travels with every clone.
A repo without the marker sees no changes and no message.
A foreign pre-push hook is never replaced; the human is told what to add.

questions.prompt: A fourth tool joins Claude Code, Droid, and Codex. It reads the same plugin format, but it distrusts plugin hooks as Codex does. What must the installer add for it?
key_points: Add the tool to the installer's list; the existing package serves it unchanged.
Write the tool's trust entries for the hooks, as the installer does for Codex.
Without the trust step, the hooks install but never run there.
